subject.title: Standardize async resource lifecycle management across retry/cleanup paths

question: Should OpenClaw introduce a shared async resource lifecycle primitive for retry, cleanup, plugin/channel, and gateway restart paths, and where should that boundary live?
rationale: The source proves the requested primitive is still missing, but choosing a shared plugin/runtime/gateway API is an ownership and compatibility decision rather than a mechanical repair.

options.title: Define a narrow lifecycle API
options.body: Create a maintainer-approved primitive with explicit ownership and migrate representative embedded-runner, plugin/channel, and restart cleanup paths behind it.

options.title: Keep local helpers
options.body: Document the existing per-surface helper pattern and close this tracker if maintainers prefer no shared cross-boundary resource manager.

options.title: Defer to concrete failures
options.body: Leave scoped fixes to new reproducible bugs and avoid adding a shared abstraction until another current-main failure proves it is needed.

recommendation.title: Define a narrow lifecycle API
recommendation.body: Create a maintainer-approved primitive with explicit ownership and migrate representative embedded-runner, plugin/channel, and restart cleanup paths behind it.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans the same lifecycle and API-boundary surfaces where this person appears as the strongest recent routing signal.
